title: Unimodality conjecture for totally nonnegative Grassmannian cardinalities
statement:
Let $q=p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime. For each $n$, consider the sequence

$$
\left(|\operatorname{Gr}_{k,n}^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{F}_q)|\right)_{0\leq k\leq n},
$$

where $\operatorname{Gr}_{k,n}^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ denotes the totally nonnegative Grassmannian over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The sequence

$$
\left(|\operatorname{Gr}_{k,n}^{\geq 0}(\mathbb{F}_q)|\right)_{0\leq k\leq n}
$$

is unimodal (log-concave). The sequence is already known to be palindromic, and log-concavity would imply unimodality because all its cardinalities are nonzero; establishing this property is the proposed extension of the corresponding familiar behavior for ordinary Grassmannian cardinalities.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06177

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
source_name: John Machacek, “A finite totally nonnegative Grassmannian”, arXiv:2410.06177 (2025).
